sentences.text: The type specimen stands about 30 cm high and is estimated to be 90 cm long, though the total length is unknown due to incomplete tail vertebrae.
It possessed a long, three-fingered hand with a partially opposable thumb featuring a recurved claw.
Nqwebasaurus represents the oldest known coelurosaur dinosaur found in Africa.
The type specimen was discovered in July 1996 by William J. de Klerk and Callum Ross during a joint expedition in the Kirkwood Formation.
The genus name comes from the Xhosa word for the Kirkwood district, and the species name means "fast runner" in ancient Xhosa.
The dinosaur lacked serrations on its upper teeth, had reduced dentition, and contained gastroliths in its abdominal cavity.
Based on its morphology, including reduced teeth and gastroliths, it is believed to have been a herbivore.
It is accepted that Nqwebasaurus likely had at least partial feathers or a feather coat for thermoregulation, similar to basal theropods.
Recent analyses place Nqwebasaurus as the most basal member of the Ornithomimosauria clade.
Nqwebasaurus lived approximately 145 to 140 million years ago during the Berriasian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Africa.
The fossil record indicates Nqwebasaurus lived between 143.1 and 132.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether Nqwebasaurus belongs to Ornithomimosauria or represents a basal compsognathid or alvarezsaurid, as older studies suggested different positions.
